analysis.title: AI and the neutral rate: Live and let rise (Top of Mind, 5 November 2026)
key_insights: ABN AMRO argues AI raises the real neutral rate (r*) in two phases. During the build-out (roughly 2026-30), r* rises because firms want to invest more than the economy wants to save. Afterwards, who receives the productivity gains determines how much higher r* stays.

Build-out: AI investment of around 3% of GDP a year adds about 0.2 pp to the US neutral rate over 2026-30, but not beyond. The US neutral rate rises to about 1.2% and the euro area's to about 0.1%. Both lifts fade once the build-out ends.

Consensus equity analyst forecasts put AI investment at about 3% of GDP a year over 2025-2030, roughly three times past ICT booms. Capex growth slows from more than 70% to around 40% in 2027, but the level keeps rising.

In Q3, investment in information processing equipment and software added 1.1 pp to US GDP growth of 3.4%. Over the past four quarters it accounts for close to half of US growth, with some import offsets.

Information processing equipment prices were falling 5-10% a year in 2019-20 and into late 2025, but have turned up to +15.7% in September as data centres absorb memory and components. Producer prices of switchgear and power transformers are up about 90% since 2019, against 26% in core consumer prices. ABN AMRO says this argues for higher policy rates over the next year or two, not a higher r*.
Hyperscaler capex absorbed 70% of operating cash flow in 2025, up from about 40% in 2018-2020. Combined debt of the five largest roughly doubled to USD 503bn in the year to September 2026.

In the year to September 2026 hyperscalers added USD 261bn of debt against USD 1.4 trillion of net new Treasury supply held by the public, about a fifth. Of the USD 288bn of bonds issued, 59% runs ten years or more. Beyond ten years they added 40% as much debt as the Treasury, and beyond 15 years they were the only source of new supply.

Market test: on 21 AI capex news days the 2-year yield moves 2.4 bp and the 10-year 1.3 bp in the direction of the news, while the 5y5y real forward rate (the market proxy for long-run r*) does not move on average.

On the ten largest hyperscaler bond deal days, the 10-year yield rose about 2 bp and the term premium 1-1.5 bp, but the 2-year rose almost as much. ABN AMRO reads this as dealers hedging new issues, not a lasting repricing of duration. Markets treat the build-out as a reason for higher policy rates for a few years, not evidence of a higher long-run r*.

Productivity phase: using the OECD's US range of 0.4 pp (low) to 0.9 pp (high) of extra annual labour productivity growth, large broadly shared gains add about 0.8 pp to US r* by the mid-2030s. If concentrated, extra saving offsets almost all of that. Smaller gains add about 0.3 pp if shared and nothing if concentrated.

Concentrated gains raise saving by 0.5-2% of GDP, assuming a 2-5 pp fall in labour share, a 20-30 pp higher saving rate on income shifted to capital owners, and precautionary saving by workers at risk of displacement. Falling compute prices could later offset part of the capital-deepening push on r*.

A bust is the main downside. Capex 1-2% of GDP below plan for two to three years removes the 0.2 pp lift and takes US r* back to about 0.9% at the central trough and about 0% in the euro area. The Fed would follow r* down faster than the ECB, and term premium pressure eases as AI firms stop issuing. It is not the near-term base case.

Euro area gets little of the build-out lift. The combined AI, defence and clean energy capex impulse in 2027 is about 1.6% of GDP in the US versus 0.3% in the EU. US r* is around 1.0% and euro area r* close to zero, a gap of about 0.9 pp that has widened since 2023.

Euro area residents bought EUR 409bn of US securities in the four quarters to Q3 2025 (2.6% of GDP, above the 1.8% current account surplus), roughly half into equities. This helps fund the US build-out and leaves euro area rates largely untouched.

Euro area rates barely react to AI news. On the average AI capex news day expected ECB rates rise 0.9 bp and the 10-year 0.5 bp, neither significant. Since 2015 about 60% of monthly changes in the US term premium reach the euro area, and about half of the euro area's 108 bp rise since late 2022 came from the US.

Backdrop: other capex, demographics and climate together add about 0.25 pp to r* in both regions from the mid-2030s. Ranges are -0.15 to +0.65 pp for the US and -0.05 to +0.55 pp for the euro area. Ageing, public debt and other capex outweigh climate.

Base case: build-out followed by a slow-burn or winner-takes-all productivity phase. US long-run r* settles at 1.4-1.6% by the mid-2030s (nominal neutral 3.4-3.6%), at or slightly above the Fed's longer-run projection of 3.2%. Euro area r* ends at 0.4-0.6% (nominal 2.4-2.6%). Only a broad boom takes US r* to about 2% and the euro area to about 1%.

Surveys put the long-run policy rate at 3.25% for the Fed and 2.0% for the ECB (real about 1.25% and 0%), below ABN AMRO's estimates. Market forwards are 5.2% for the US 5y5y and 3.6% for the euro area, above even a broad boom, but include a term premium. Squaring forwards with the base case needs a term premium of about 1.7 pp in the US and 1.1 pp in the euro area.

The 1995-2004 US productivity boom: HLW r* rose from 2.5% to 3.9% by 2000 and fell back to about 2.6% by 2003, tracking the investment-saving gap rather than productivity. A Taylor rule letting r* rise pointed to policy rates of 5-6% in the late 1990s against about 4% with r* fixed at 2%. If AI lifts r*, an unchanged policy rate is looser than it looks.

macro_indicators.interpretation: At or slightly above the Fed's longer-run projection of 3.2%.
Only broadly shared AI productivity gains lift long-run US r* clearly.

Euro area gets little of the build-out lift. About 1% only in a broad boom.

Above even a broad boom (about 4% nominal) but includes a term premium. Implied term premium of about 1.7 pp to square with ABN AMRO's base case.

risk_factors: A boom-bust path: capex cut 1-2% of GDP below plan for two to three years would take US r* back to about 0.9% and euro area r* to about 0%. ABN AMRO sees a meaningful chance of it, though not in the near term.
Concentrated AI gains raise saving and leave long-run r* ambiguous, and could weaken tax revenues and add to transfer needs.
Rising hyperscaler debt issuance, with capex running ahead of cash flow, could push up the term premium.
Compute prices resuming their fall could offset part of the capital-deepening push on r*.
A lasting climate hit to productivity pulls r* down by an estimated 0.1-0.2 pp by the mid-2030s.

On the ten largest hyperscaler bond deal days the 10-year yield rose about 2 bp and the term premium 1-1.5 bp, with the 2-year rising almost as much, which ABN AMRO attributes to dealer hedging of new issues.

Hyperscaler debt issuance is about a fifth of net new Treasury supply, and beyond 15 years it was the only source of new supply. ABN AMRO expects the term premium to start rising if AI firms keep borrowing at this pace.

tension_points.bull_case: Broadly shared productivity gains of 0.9 pp a year add about 0.8 pp to US r* and take it to about 2% by the mid-2030s. Market forwards (US 5y5y 5.2%) already sit above even this path.
tension_points.bear_case: Concentrated gains raise saving by 0.5-2% of GDP and offset almost all of the lift, leaving r* at 1.4-1.6%. A capex bust would take r* back to about 0.9%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 5y5y real forward rate staying unchanged on AI capex news days, and the term premium not rising despite continued hyperscaler borrowing, would show markets pricing no lasting lift.

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI build-out raises r* while it lasts, which keeps policy rates higher for a few years but does not yet show in long-run real rates.
theme_stances.evidence: The build-out lifts r* while it lasts.

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscaler borrowing is a growing share of long-dated supply and should raise the term premium if it continues.
theme_stances.evidence: If AI firms keep borrowing at this pace, the term premium should also start to rise.
